launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.address: 4135 W Lake Harriet Parkway, Minneapolis, MN 55409
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.summary: Minneapolis's signature lake district linking Bde Maka Ska, Lake Harriet, Lake of the Isles, Cedar Lake, Brownie Lake, beaches, gardens, bandshell, paddling, fishing, winter trails, and separated walking and biking loops.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.hours: Developed park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m.-midnight and undeveloped areas 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Beaches, rentals, concessions, concerts, streetcar, ice rinks, and gardens keep seasonal schedules.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.parking: Pay lots and metered parkway spaces serve major beaches and Lake Harriet; neighborhood curb access varies. Warm weekends and concerts fill the closest spaces, so route to the exact lake feature or arrive by bike or transit.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.arrival: This is a multi-lake regional park, not one entrance. Choose Bde Maka Ska for active water recreation, Lake Harriet for bandshell and family facilities, Lake of the Isles for scenic loops, or Cedar Lake for quieter beaches.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.restrooms: Restrooms, fountains, and wells are concentrated near beaches, pavilions, and developed nodes and may be seasonal. Do not expect an open facility on every loop segment.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.cost: Lakes, trails, beaches, gardens, and ordinary park use are free. Parking, rentals, food, streetcar rides, permits, and some programs cost separately.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.accessibility: Paved lake loops and developed beach or pavilion areas offer accessible options, but construction, winter snow, sand, older docks, trail detours, and natural shore edges vary.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.dogs: Leash dogs in ordinary park areas and keep them out of guarded swimming zones, playgrounds, gardens, and posted sensitive areas. Use separately designated dog parks for off-leash activity.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.family: Beaches, playgrounds, boats, bandshell events, gardens, paths, and the streetcar provide strong family choices. Select one lake zone and verify water quality, lifeguard, rental, and concession status.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.transit: Metro Transit buses, biking, walking, rideshare, and connected regional trails serve the lakes. Bike travel between destinations is often easier than relocating a car.
launch-mn-minneapolis-chain-of-lakes-reg.need: Lake Harriet bandshell and shoreline work can alter paths and facilities. Check beach water quality, algae notices, concert schedules, winter ice status, trail detours, and current construction before a feature-specific trip.

launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.summary: A nationally known Mississippi tributary park centered on 53-foot Minnehaha Falls, with gorge trails, gardens, historic buildings, public art, playground, seasonal wading pool, picnics, Sea Salt Eatery, disc golf, and links toward Fort Snelling.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.hours: Developed areas are open 6:00 a.m.-midnight and undeveloped areas 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Pergola Garden is 7:30 a.m.-10:00 p.m.; food, wading pool, historic sites, and rentals have separate seasonal hours.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.parking: The park has pay parking, some free lots, and metered street spaces. Route to the falls, Wabun area, Longfellow Gardens, or dog-park edge rather than assuming the closest visible lot serves every destination.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.arrival: The falls overlook is near Sea Salt and the main pavilion. Lower Glen stairs and trails descend into a steep, wet gorge; Wabun family facilities and Longfellow Gardens sit in different zones.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.restrooms: Restrooms and drinking fountains are available near the developed falls and picnic areas, with seasonal facilities elsewhere. The lower gorge itself has limited services.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.cost: Falls, gardens, trails, playground, wading pool when operating, and historic-site exteriors are free. Parking, food, rentals, reservations, and some programs cost.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.accessibility: The upper falls overlooks and major developed areas have paved access, but lower gorge trails include long stairs, steep grades, roots, mud, ice, and spray.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary park areas. The former Minnehaha off-leash area is being decommissioned; do not rely on old maps or reviews for current dog-park access.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.family: Upper overlooks, Wabun playground, wading pool, picnics, gardens, and historic buildings suit families. Closely supervise children near cliffs, creek edges, stairs, slippery rock, and fast water.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.transit: METRO Blue Line's 50th Street/Minnehaha Park station and buses provide strong car-free access; regional bike trails also connect directly.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minnehaha-regional.need: Water flow changes dramatically by season and weather, and gorge stairs become icy or slippery. Check wading-pool status, Sea Salt hours, trail closures, and the current off-leash transition before leaving.

launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.summary: A 700-plus-acre year-round recreation landscape with The Trailhead, Wirth Lake Beach, wildflower garden, quaking bog, children's garden, golf, disc golf, mountain biking, skiing, tubing, snowshoeing, trails, and skyline views.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.hours: Developed areas are generally open 6:00 a.m.-midnight and undeveloped areas 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. The Trailhead, gardens, beach, golf, rentals, ski trails, and winter operations keep separate schedules.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.parking: Use The Trailhead lots for central recreation, Wirth Beach for lake and cycling access, or the small metered garden and bog lots. Event and winter demand can fill lots; parkway shoulder parking is restricted.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.arrival: Theodore Wirth is larger than many visitors expect. Choose The Trailhead, beach, Eloise Butler garden, Quaking Bog, golf, or a winter activity before driving.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.restrooms: Restrooms are most dependable at The Trailhead and staffed seasonal facilities. Natural trails, bog paths, garden areas, and remote loops have limited services.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.cost: General park and many trails are free. Golf, ski passes, rentals, tubing, lessons, food, parking in selected lots, and events cost separately.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.accessibility: The Trailhead and developed facilities provide accessible access; natural trails, boardwalks, snow, sand, hills, and off-road cycling terrain vary widely.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.dogs: Leash dogs under park rules and keep them out of beaches, gardens, groomed ski-only routes, and posted facilities. Activity-specific restrictions apply.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.family: Beach, children's garden, easy paths, tubing, skiing, disc golf, and Trailhead facilities offer year-round choices. Match terrain and winter conditions to the youngest participant.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.transit: Metro Transit, biking via Luce Line and parkway trails, rideshare, and driving reach different park sections; no single stop serves every destination.
launch-mn-minneapolis-theodore-wirth-reg.need: Off-road trails close to all users when wet; if a foot or tire leaves a mark, stay off. Verify ski or tubing operations, beach status, garden season, trail conditions, and current Trailhead food service.

launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.summary: A 132-acre urban river gorge between Bridge 9 and Minnehaha Regional Park, with bluff-top parkways, Winchell Trail, river flats, forest, overlooks, stairs, beaches, regional trails, and rare Mississippi gorge geology.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.hours: Developed areas generally follow 6:00 a.m.-midnight hours and undeveloped natural areas 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Trail, stair, beach, flood, and construction closures may be more restrictive.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.parking: Use legal parkway or neighborhood spaces near a named access point. Many trail stairs have little or no dedicated parking, and opposite riverbanks require bridge crossings.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.arrival: Choose the west-bank Winchell Trail and numbered stair access, East River Flats near the university, Bohemian Flats, or a regional-trail segment before traveling.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.restrooms: Facilities are limited and concentrated at developed parks such as East River Flats or nearby recreation nodes. Natural gorge paths and stair accesses usually have none.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.cost: Trails, overlooks, river flats, and ordinary park access are free. Parking, reservations, rentals, and events may cost.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.accessibility: Bluff-top paved regional trails provide the most accessible experience. Winchell Trail, riverbank paths, beaches, and long stairways are steep, uneven, and seasonally muddy or icy.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.dogs: Leash dogs and keep them on designated paths; steep bluffs, wildlife habitat, fast water, bikes, and narrow trails require close control.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.family: Paved river overlooks and developed flats can suit families, while Winchell Trail and gorge stairs require trail readiness and direct supervision.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.transit: Metro Transit, university routes, biking, walking, and bridge connections serve the corridor. Plan which bank you need before arrival.
launch-mn-minneapolis-mississippi-gorge-.need: River level, erosion, fallen trees, spring flooding, winter ice, and stair maintenance can change access quickly. Do not climb closed slopes or treat informal river edges as guarded beaches.

launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.summary: A free 11-acre outdoor art destination beside Walker Art Center with Spoonbridge and Cherry, major contemporary sculptures, native plantings, accessible paths, skyline views, digital guide, seasonal family programs, and year-round public access.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.hours: The Sculpture Garden is free and open daily 6:00 a.m.-midnight year-round. Walker galleries, cafe, restrooms, tours, programs, and indoor services keep shorter schedules and holiday closures.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.parking: Paid underground parking is entered from Vineland Place, with nearby metered streets and a surface lot. Accessible spaces are on ramp level P1 with a direct Walker connection.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.arrival: Garden entrances are on Vineland Place and Bryant Avenue. Start near Spoonbridge and Cherry for the lower garden or use the switchback path for the Wurtele Upper Garden and Walker campus.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.restrooms: Dependable public restrooms are inside Walker Art Center during gallery hours; the outdoor garden remains open much longer, so plan accordingly.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.cost: The Sculpture Garden and digital guide are always free. Walker gallery admission for adults, parking, cafe purchases, private tours, performances, and events cost separately; visitors 18 and under enter Walker galleries free.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.accessibility: Accessible entrances, paved central and perimeter paths, and a switchback route serve the garden. Some sculptures and programs require crossing grass or gravel surfaces.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.dogs: Leashed dogs may use outdoor public paths under posted rules, but only service animals enter Walker indoor spaces. Keep animals away from artworks and planted beds.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.family: Iconic sculptures, free digital interpretation, lawns, and summer art-making make an easy family visit. Children may look closely but must not climb or touch works unless signage permits.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.transit: Metro Transit lines 4, 25, and E Line stop within a short walk; biking, walking from Loring Park, rideshare, and paid parking are straightforward.
launch-mn-minneapolis-minneapolis-sculpt.need: The outdoor garden's hours do not mean the museum, cafe, restrooms, or visitor desk are open. Check weather and program updates, and use the official digital guide rather than relying on outdated artwork lists.

launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.summary: Saint Paul's major all-ages destination combining free Como Zoo and conservatory, Japanese garden, Como Lake, pavilion, playground, carousel, amusement park, pool, golf, woodland classroom, trails, picnics, and winter recreation.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.hours: The outdoor regional park is open sunrise-11:00 p.m. Zoo, conservatory, Japanese garden, Como Town, carousel, pool, pavilion restaurant, golf, rentals, and ski center all keep separate schedules.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.parking: Free lots and streets are distributed around the zoo campus, lake, pool, picnic areas, golf, and athletic fields. Zoo and conservatory parking fills on weekends; route to the exact facility and consider transit.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.arrival: The zoo/conservatory campus, lake pavilion, Como Town, pool, golf course, woodland classroom, and picnic zones are separate. Walking between them can be much farther than the map appears.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available at staffed attractions and selected seasonal park facilities. Outdoor restrooms and water features may close seasonally.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.cost: The park, Como Zoo, conservatory, and Japanese garden are free with donations encouraged. Como Town rides, carousel, pool, golf, rentals, food, parking violations, and programs cost separately.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.accessibility: Major attractions and paved lake routes provide accessible options; historic paths, crowded buildings, snow, shoreline, and amusement rides vary.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary park areas but not zoo, conservatory, pool, play equipment, food interiors, or other posted facilities. Service-animal rules differ inside attractions.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.family: Free animals and gardens plus rides, carousel, pool, playground, lake, food, and picnics make this a full-day family destination. Set expectations about separate ride and pool costs.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.transit: Metro Transit buses, biking, walking, rideshare, and driving serve multiple edges. Event days and warm weekends favor transit or early arrival.
launch-mn-st-paul-como-regional-park.need: Do not apply park hours to the zoo or conservatory. Check attraction hours, plant or animal building closures, Como Town season, pool status, parking projects, and winter operations before traveling.

launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.summary: A large East Side lake park with guarded beach, free splash pad, China Garden, three-mile paved loop, playground, boating, fishing, golf, amphitheater, picnic island, pavilion, sports, seasonal restrooms, and winter trails.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.hours: The park is open sunrise-11:00 p.m. In 2026 the guarded beach is weather permitting through September 7, generally noon-8:00 p.m. before August and noon-7:00 p.m. later; splash pad runs 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. June 13-September 7.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.parking: Free parking serves the beach and other developed areas, but the lake is large. Route to beach, China Garden, picnic pavilion, golf, boat launch, or recreation center rather than one center pin.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.arrival: The beach and splash pad are on one shore, the public boat launch is at the north end, China Garden and pavilion occupy distinct zones, and the paved loop circles the lake.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.restrooms: Changing rooms and restrooms serve the guarded beach, while other park restrooms are seasonal. Confirm availability outside beach hours or winter season.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.cost: Park, beach admission, parking, splash pad, playground, loop trail, China Garden, and ordinary picnics are free. Watercraft rentals, golf, storage, lessons, reservations, and concessions cost.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.accessibility: Paved lake routes, beach facilities, parking, and developed recreation areas provide accessible options; sand, docks, snow, ice, and garden terrain vary.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.dogs: Leash dogs in ordinary park areas and keep them out of the guarded beach, splash pad, playground, golf course, buildings, and posted garden areas.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.family: Free guarded swimming, splash pad, playground, changing rooms, lake loop, boats, picnics, and garden make this a strong summer family destination.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.transit: Metro Transit buses, biking, walking, rideshare, and free parking serve different park edges. Select the nearest destination entrance first.
launch-mn-st-paul-phalen-regional-park.need: Beach and splash-pad operation is weather, staffing, and water-quality dependent. Youth under 12 require an accompanying adult; check current closures, swim rules, and rental status before leaving.

launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.address: 200 Dr Justus Ohage Boulevard, Saint Paul, MN 55107
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.summary: A Mississippi riverfront destination facing downtown Saint Paul with broad event lawns, Wigington Pavilion, Target Stage, picnic shelter, public dock, riverwalk, play area, bike connections, cruises, and access toward Raspberry Island.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.hours: General Saint Paul park hours are sunrise-11:00 p.m.; reserved pavilions, stages, docks, cruises, restrooms, event enclosures, and adjacent island spaces follow separate schedules.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.parking: Surface lots and event parking serve Harriet Island, but festivals, concerts, floods, and private rentals can close roads or reserve spaces. Use the exact event or facility entrance.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.arrival: Dr. Justus Ohage Boulevard reaches the main island. Wigington Pavilion, Target Stage, Kelley's Landing, public dock, play area, Raspberry Island, and riverboat boarding are separate destinations.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.restrooms: Restrooms are seasonal, with additional facilities during events or inside reserved buildings. Do not expect public access inside a private pavilion rental.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.cost: Park lawns, riverwalk, skyline views, play area, and ordinary picnics are free. Parking during some events, pavilion rentals, cruises, festivals, food, and programs cost.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.accessibility: Paved riverwalk and developed event facilities provide accessible routes, but flood closures, grass event fields, docks, snow, and bridge grades can affect access.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.dogs: Leash dogs and keep them out of private events, play equipment, food areas, and posted docks or facilities. Crowds, fireworks, heat, and river edges add risk.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.family: Skyline views, boats, lawns, play area, picnics, riverwalk, and festivals can suit families. Supervise continuously near docks and the Mississippi River.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.transit: Biking via regional trails, walking from downtown bridges, Metro Transit, rideshare, and driving are options. Bridge grades and event street closures matter.
launch-mn-st-paul-harriet-island-regiona.need: Harriet Island is both a daily park and major event venue. Check the event calendar, pavilion rentals, flood or river conditions, dock access, road closures, and seasonal restrooms before a specific visit.
